name: Perun
role: God of thunder, lightning and the oak
fun_fact: Oaths in the Primary Chronicle were sworn by Perun and Veles together, which is one reason scholars pair them.

name: Veles
role: God of cattle, waters and the underworld
fun_fact: Veles is often reconstructed as Perun's opponent, yet the Primary Chronicle names him in the same oath formula as Perun.

name: Ivan Tsarevich
role: Youngest tsar's son and hero of the firebird quest
fun_fact: In Afanasyev's version Ivan wins not by strength but by listening to the grey wolf, whose warnings he keeps forgetting.

name: Firebird
role: Glowing bird whose feather begins the quest
fun_fact: The firebird's light is so bright that a single feather can illuminate a whole room, and the tale never lets the bird be simply caught.

name: Grey Wolf
role: Shape-shifting helper and guide to Ivan
fun_fact: In many tellings the wolf first eats Ivan's horse, then repays him by carrying him across the whole quest.

name: Vasilisa
role: Brave girl who outwits Baba Yaga
fun_fact: Vasilisa's doll must be fed and kept secret, a small domestic ritual that keeps her mother's care alive in the forest.

name: Baba Yaga
role: Ambiguous crone and guardian of the forest threshold
fun_fact: Baba Yaga flies in a mortar and sweeps her trail with a broom, and in some tales she is a helper rather than a threat.

name: Ilya Muromets
role: Bogatyr of Murom and defender of Kyiv
fun_fact: Ilya sat unable to walk for thirty-three years before pilgrims healed him, and he became the most popular hero of the Russian byliny.

name: Rusalka
role: Water spirit of the drowned and the untimely dead
fun_fact: Rusalki were sometimes honoured with songs and bread rather than feared, and their week could be a time of courtship as well as danger.

name: Morozko
role: Winter spirit who tests and rewards
fun_fact: Morozko is often identified with Ded Moroz, the Russian Father Frost, though the gift-bringer of New Year celebrations is a later, softer figure.
